state_request_queue.block_index_rule: off / 4, minus the block count once when it is not smaller (004e4486, 004d3eff)

enqueue.argument: pointer to the int to copy, loaded at 004d3f35; call sites push the address of a stack slot, not a literal
enqueue.grow_condition: (head + count) % 4 == 0 and block count not greater than (count + 4) / 4
enqueue.ledger_correction: the existing 004d3ed0 record calls the element 10h bytes; 10h is the block size and the element is a 4-byte int. 004d3ed0 is outside this packet's lease so the record was not edited.

grow.rotation: blocks are moved so the sequence starting at the head block stays contiguous and the new slots fall behind it; both native branches 004d216d and 004d21a7 produce the same modular rotation
grow.head_offset_untouched: 004d2211 adds only to the block count, unlike the usual _Growmap

pop_front.rule: head += 1; head = 0 when it reaches block_count * 4; count -= 1; head = 0 when the queue empties; blocks are never released

drain.gate: OnMove drains only when game+5ECh is zero, 004e4d02
drain.ordering_rule: first in first out; the count is re-read at 004e4866 after every handler, so a request a handler enqueues is serviced in the same pass behind everything already queued

callees.name: BSP_Game_UpdateCutscenePlayback
callees.position: 004e4d6d, immediately after the frame clock accumulate, with the delta slot 004c6e30 rewrote
callees.gate: game+634h == 0 || game+635h != 0, the same condition as the simulation gate at 004e50b0
callees.behaviour: with an object at game+38h calls 00425d10(0) then 00530630; unless the object's +60h is 4 it either tears it down (004c43c0 action 3 pressed: 0045f600, 004bea40 on a stack copy, game+38h = 0) or advances it with the raw delta through 0045f970

callees.name: BSP_FrameStats_Accumulate
callees.abi: __thiscall, ECX = game+19C8h (the value, not the game object), no arguments
callees.map_correction: the OnMove map lists it under GUI/text; the call site loads game+19C8h into ECX so it is a separate object
callees.behaviour: reads profiler counter slots 0109d014, 0109db08, 0109db34 and 0109db14 out of the profiler array at instance+20h and accumulates into this+68h, +6Ch, +70h and +74h with a sample counter at +78h

callees.name: BSP_Game_UpdatePresenceContext
callees.behaviour: takes the wall clock from 01090ab0 vtable +20h (two int64s divided on the x87 stack, ticks over frequency), compares against 00e18b30, and does nothing until 3.0 s (00d7a2b0) have passed; past that it calls XUserSetContext and XUserSetContextEx (00a4d3f2, 00a4d41c) with context 8001h among others
callees.significance: second confirmation that 01090ab0 is the frame clock object

callees.name: BSP_Game_UpdateDeviceWaitScreen
callees.behaviour: with mode 0 or the scene flag at game+1EF0h+29Ch clear it polls the input backend 00f8bbf4 through 00a91020, latches at backend+DDh, and on a rising edge with the menu (00425d10 +25Ch) and GUI (00f8abe8 +3E8h) idle calls BSP_InputManager_Update(0.0f); in mode 1 it counts the game+18CCh slots with the +9h and +0Eh tests and, when fewer than two are active or game+624h is zero, builds a stack event through 0075b430 and dispatches it into the scene at game+1EF0h through 0076a9f0 and 007848f0; both branches end in 004da6c0

callees.name: BSP_Game_CheckMissionCompletion
callees.behaviour: three zero-delta ticks of the world at game+19CCh through its vtable +Ch with 00903670 between them, then 004c3cb0(game) and the result GUI through 004f8a20 and 004f8970 on 00e18d48 using the float at result+8h and the record at result+14h; if result+21h is set it enqueues 0Fh and sets game+5ECh to 1; ends with 004cd610(game, 1) and a tail jump to 004cc510 with ECX = &game+7188h, a pointer to the slot rather than the object
